clue.text: US politician's annoyed comment about rebuffed advance

indicators.note: the exclamation sits about, i.e. around, the turned word

parts.note: drat is an exclamation of mild annoyance

indicators.note: rebuffed means pushed back, so the word for advance is read backwards

parts.note: to advance is to come forward

explanation.surface: A grumble from an American politician whose overture was turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is only 'US politician'; the 's is a link word, read as 'has'. 'about' is the container signal and 'rebuffed' the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of one of the two main American parties is a politician of that country.

clue.text: Met up, getting less potent drink

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: met, as in confronted, is faced

explanation.surface: People met up and chose a weaker drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FACED into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee with the caffeine removed is a drink with less kick.

clue.text: Japanese writer, male — his aim is astray

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so the letters of his aim wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A Japanese author, a man, whose goal has gone off target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' is the anagram signal for 'his aim'; 'is' is a link word. Yukio Mishima wrote The Sea of Fertility.
explanation.definitionFit: Yukio Mishima was a celebrated twentieth-century Japanese novelist and playwright.

clue.text: Beethoven work? Tough work, almost (not quite entirely)

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short

parts.note: a chore is an onerous task

indicators.note: not quite means the word for entirely loses its final letter

parts.note: all means entirely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: Asks whether a piece by Beethoven is hard labour, nearly but not totally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts CHORE to CHOR and 'not quite' cuts ALL to AL. The question mark flags a definition by example: the Choral Symphony is Beethoven's Ninth.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Ninth Symphony is nicknamed the Choral, so the name serves as one of his pieces.

clue.text: What erotica may do in a ploy securing love

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the letters for a ploy hold the zero inside them

parts.note: a ruse is a ploy or trick
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: Erotic writing as a crafty means of winning someone's affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'securing' puts O inside A RUSE, after its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Racy material is meant to excite desire, which is to stir or stimulate.

clue.text: Some reconsideration is sensible for military designer

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Thinking again would be wise for someone designing for the army.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'for'; 'for' is only a link word, so the definition is 'military designer'. Peter Nissen designed the corrugated-iron Nissen hut used by the army.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Nissen was the engineer behind the semicircular hut used widely by armed forces in both world wars.

clue.text: Mathematical quantity: some number in it turning huge

indicators.note: in means the letter for a number goes inside the word it

parts.note: taken as written
N stands for an unspecified number in mathematics

indicators.note: turning means the word for huge is read backwards

parts.note: large means huge

explanation.surface: A maths quantity, where some figure grows enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some number' is N, the algebraic stand-in for any number; 'in' and 'turning' are the container and reversal signals.
explanation.definitionFit: In calculus the result of integrating a function is itself a quantity with that name.

clue.text: Nut, alas, misrepresents this form of fruit

indicators.note: to misrepresent is to present wrongly, so the letters of nut and alas are presented in a different order

explanation.surface: A sigh that a nut is wrongly portrayed as some kind of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misrepresents' rearranges NUTALAS; 'this' points back to the anagram's result.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultana is a dried seedless grape, a kind of dried fruit.

clue.text: Was sent abroad — Midwest state — for source of information

indicators.note: abroad here means scattered widely, so the letters of was sent are spread into a new order

parts.note: ND is the postal abbreviation for North Dakota, a Midwestern US state

explanation.surface: Someone was posted overseas, to a Midwestern state, to find out what is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' signals the anagram of 'Was sent'; North Dakota supplies the last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiosk selling papers and magazines is where people get their news.

clue.text: Awful time getting away from secure locations

indicators.note: getting away from means the letter for time escapes from the longer word

parts.note: hideouts are safe places to lie low

explanation.surface: A dreadful period spent escaping from safe houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting away from' removes T from HIDEOUTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something dreadful or very ugly.

clue.text: Universal expert is confounded with gloom, beset by expense

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the word for expense goes round the jumble

parts.note: an expense is a cost

indicators.note: confounded means thrown into confusion, so the letters of is and gloom are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A specialist is miserably low-spirited and swamped by costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Universal' looks like an adjective of scope but means 'of the universe'. 'confounded' is the anagram signal and 'beset by' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who studies the origin and structure of the universe is an expert in all things universal.

clue.text: Underhand punch, knocking head off

indicators.note: knocking the head off removes the first letter

parts.note: a blow is a punch

explanation.surface: A sneaky punch that knocks someone's head off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking head off' takes B from BLOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Low as in a low trick means mean or devious, the same as underhand.

clue.text: Hot food? Safer with ices, possibly

indicators.note: possibly means the letters might be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks whether hot food is less risky when served with ice creams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges SAFERICES.
explanation.definitionFit: A stew of meat in a white sauce, served warm, is a hot dish.

clue.text: Mirror left amidst vapour (sulphur)

indicators.note: amidst means the letter for left sits inside the word for vapour

parts.note: gas is a vapour
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A mirror on the left in sulphurous fumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amidst' puts L inside GAS, after its G, and S follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A looking glass is a mirror, and glass alone is used in the same sense.

clue.text: One brought in by rigged constituency

indicators.note: brought in by means the letter for one is placed inside the word for rigged

parts.note: set, as in fixed or set up, means rigged
a means one, as in a single

explanation.surface: A single candidate elected thanks to a fixed electoral district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in by' puts A inside SET.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliamentary seat is the constituency an MP represents.

clue.text: Dismiss clergy making show of repentance?

parts.note: to sack is to dismiss from a job
the cloth is the clergy collectively

explanation.surface: Wonders whether firing the clergy counts as repenting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cloth' means the clergy. Wearing sackcloth and ashes is the traditional sign of penitence.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough garment worn as a sign of penitence, as in the phrase sackcloth and ashes.

clue.text: Vegetable i.e. a bit of broccoli between furrow and stove

parts.note: a rut is a groove or furrow

indicators.note: a bit of the word broccoli is its first letter

parts.note: an Aga is a make of cast-iron cooking stove

explanation.surface: A vegetable described as a piece of broccoli sitting between a ditch and the cooker.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a heavy cast-iron range cooker found in many British country kitchens. 'i.e.' is a link word, and 'between' sets the middle pieces inside the outer two.
explanation.definitionFit: The rutabaga is the American name for the swede, a root vegetable.

clue.text: Flowering plant, a symbol of love aboard the Underground

indicators.note: aboard means riding on, so the symbol of love comes on after the Underground

parts.note: the Tube is London's Underground railway
a red rose is the classic token of love

explanation.surface: Someone carries a romantic flower on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The TUBE is the popular name for the London Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuberose is a fragrant white-flowered plant grown for perfume.

clue.text: Politician, one investing in evasive business

indicators.note: investing means surrounding, so the politician and one go inside the word for evasive

parts.note: coy means reluctant to give details, evasive
MP is a Member of Parliament
an means one, as in an apple

explanation.surface: A politician puts money into a business that is cagey about its affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing in' reads like finance but is the container signal: to invest is also to surround.
explanation.definitionFit: A company is a commercial firm, a business.

clue.text: Find voucher in possession of the writer? Just the reverse

indicators.note: in possession of seems to put the voucher inside the writer's word
just the reverse flips the containment, so the writer's word goes inside the voucher instead

parts.note: a coupon is a voucher
the writer is the setter, referring to himself as me

explanation.surface: Locate a voucher that the setter owns, or rather the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in possession of' would put the voucher inside the writer; 'Just the reverse' tells you to swap which piece holds which.
explanation.definitionFit: To come upon something is to find it by chance.

clue.text: Worker in health club post mostly regrets turning up

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a mast is a tall post

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is written backwards, bottom to top

parts.note: rues means regrets

explanation.surface: A spa employee regrets nearly every arriving letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts MAST to MAS; 'turning up' makes SEUR from RUES.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who gives massages works at spas and gyms.

clue.text: Hackneyed thought millions ignored

indicators.note: ignored means the letter for millions is left out

parts.note: mused means thought or pondered

explanation.surface: An idea is stale and the millions it involves are overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' takes M from MUSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overused and worn out is hackneyed, like a stale phrase.

clue.text: Intellectual discipline that is presented in different ways — note church following

indicators.note: following means the church abbreviation comes after the note

parts.words: that is presented in different ways
parts.note: that is can be shortened two ways, sc from Latin scilicet and ie from Latin id est, and both are given
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A field of study offered in assorted forms, with a musical note and a church to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' is given in two abbreviations, SC (scilicet) and IE (id est), joined as SCIE. CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A systematic field of study, such as physics or chemistry, is an intellectual discipline.

clue.text: Substantial protection against collisions

definitions.meaning: ... means very large, as in a ... harvest
a car's bar at front and back that absorbs knocks

explanation.surface: Solid, heavy-duty crash protection.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumper crop is a big one, and the car part guards against impacts.

clue.text: Old Mexican almost informed Private Eye

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: told means informed
a private eye is a detective, shortened to tec

explanation.surface: An ancient Mexican nearly briefed a private investigator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts TOLD to TOL. 'Private Eye' looks like the British satirical magazine but means a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: The Toltecs were a people who dominated central Mexico before the Aztecs.

clue.text: Class and so on backed accepting a school's head

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the reversed letters hold the a and the school's first letter
backed means moved backwards, so the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: etc means and so on

indicators.note: the head of the word school is its first letter

explanation.surface: A school class, its head taken on, and so forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns ETC into CTE, and 'accepting' puts AS inside it after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social class, especially in Hindu society.

clue.text: Underworld attack with gun mostly shocked nation

indicators.note: mostly means the slang word loses its last letter

parts.note: to plug someone is slang for shooting them

indicators.note: shocked means jolted into disorder, so the letters of nation are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gangland shooting leaves the country stunned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts PLUG to PLU, and 'shocked' turns NATION into TONIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluto ruled the Roman underworld, so things belonging to the infernal regions take his name as an adjective.

clue.text: Poor of Parisian, gripped by desire, to pop up

indicators.note: in a down clue, popping up means the letters are read from the bottom upward, backwards
gripped by means the French word is held inside the word for desire

parts.note: a yen is a longing or desire
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A poor Frenchman, gripped by longing, keeps appearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripped by' makes YDEEN, which 'to pop up' reverses, as a down entry is read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Being poor means being in want, lacking the necessities of life.

clue.text: Poetic form and style not initially mastered

indicators.note: not means the letter that follows is left out of the word for style

parts.note: a mode is a style or manner

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of mastered

explanation.surface: A type of verse whose style has not yet been perfected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives M, which 'not' removes from MODE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem addressed to a subject, a recognised form of verse.

clue.text: Great influence? I cope not with men, sadly

indicators.note: sadly, as in badly or poorly, says these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A confession of being unable to deal with men, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges ICOPENOTMEN. The question mark marks the definition as an understatement.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlimited power is the greatest influence one could have, so the definition understates it.

clue.text: Woman's particular individuals, nameless objects of reverence

parts.note: her means belonging to a woman

indicators.note: nameless means without the N that stands for name

parts.note: ones, as in the little ones, means particular individuals

explanation.surface: A woman's specific people, unnamed, whom she reveres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' removes N, the abbreviation for name; 'particular individuals' means ones, as in 'the ones I meant'.
explanation.definitionFit: Admired champions are revered and looked up to.

clue.text: Dishes Capability's first element of garden design

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of Capability

parts.note: a rockery is a garden feature of stones and plants

explanation.surface: Dishes as the first element in a Capability Brown garden design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capability' suggests Capability Brown, the famous English landscape gardener, but supplies only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Plates, cups and bowls are collectively the dishes or crockery.
